catalyst_3.title: Verify
catalyst_3.evidence: Kill attempt FAILED on the event itself — all load-bearing facts verified primary: $8.11 cash + 0.2215 New CommerceOne shares, Smith Ventures $690M for the non-bank Payments business (of which $470M to holders, $155M into the bank, $65M debt paydown), both shareholder bases approved 2026-06-23 (>99% GDOT / 100% CommerceOne), and the ONLY outstanding gates are the Federal Reserve, Alabama State Banking Dept and Utah DFI with a Q3 2026 target — no approval announced as of 2026-07-20, so the event is genuinely forward and un-fired. Live quote confirms $13.40 exactly. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) The line mischaracterizes the $14.23-$19.18 band as "the sponsor's" valuation implying a $6.12-$11.07 stub floor. It is not a sponsor mark — the DEFM14A/425 states it is an ILLUSTRATIVE sensitivity at an assumed ~1.00x-1.80x tangible book value multiple. The LOW end already assumes 1.0x TBV, so there is no floor at all: an unlisted small-cap bank holdco can and often does open below 1.0x TBV, meaning $13.40 is not provably a discount to intrinsic — the entire gap is an unpriceable stub-multiple bet, which is weaker than the "arb" framing. (2) Timing risk is understated: the close target has ALREADY slipped once, from the Q2 2026 guided at the November 2025 announcement to the current Q3 2026 — the slip the line treats as a hypothetical risk has already happened, and only ~10 weeks of Q3 remain with three separate regulators outstanding. Tradeability is otherwise clean (NYSE, ~$760M cap, ~250k shares/day) and the line honestly self-discloses the un-hedgeable stub leg. Score trimmed 7 to 6 for the illusory floor and the demonstrated timeline slippage.

catalyst_density.rating: M — the spread is real and mechanically identifiable (price below even the low end of the illustrative consideration range), but the entire discount sits in an unlisted, unmarkable New CommerceOne stub, so "cheap" is not provable without independently underwriting a private Alabama bank holdco. Bank-regulator gating is also the slowest, least handicappable approval path, and Q3 is a target not a covenant.

catalyst_3.title: Verify
catalyst_3.evidence: Kill attempt failed on facts, succeeded only on a date nuance. PRIMARY-CONFIRMED via SEC 8-K (CIK 1162194, acc 0001104659-26-071195) + Jun-8-2026 press release: all-stock definitive merger with Treeline; LAB valued at net cash delivered at closing plus $10M (~$460M); LAB holders ~16% fully diluted of $2.5B Treeline; closing dividend of one CVR per share covering net proceeds from legacy Mass Cytometry/Microfluidics plus up to $50M of Illumina SomaLogic earnout, 5-year CVR term, paid in combined-company SHARES not cash; combined co. >$900M cash, runway into 2029, "TRLN" on Nasdaq, close 2H-2026. CORRECTION 1: the merger agreement was executed Jun-6-2026; Jun-8-2026 is the announcement date — the line's "announced Jun-8-2026" is right but the deal date is Jun-6. CORRECTION 2: CVR pays in stock of the combined company, not cash, so even a successful divestiture does not deliver cash to legacy holders — the line's "CVR rides free post-close" understates that the CVR is itself Treeline equity beta, not a cash stub. CORRECTION 3: the Illumina $50M is a carve-out of the larger $75M earnout from the Jan-30-2026 $350M-upfront/$425M-total proteomics sale; only $50M flows to the CVR. FORWARD-LEG CONFIRMED: the Mass Cytometry/Microfluidics divestiture remains unannounced — Q1-2026 10-Q and merger materials say only that Treeline does not intend to operate the units and the company is "exploring a range of opportunities, including divestitures"; no buyer, price, or timeline exists in any primary filing as of 2026-07-20. Vote date and S-4 effectiveness likewise not public (S-4 stated as intended-to-file, Treeline board and stockholders have already approved; LAB stockholder approval outstanding). TAPE VERIFIED: LAB $0.8949 (+4.36%), mkt cap $350.3M, ~391.5M shares, 52wk 0.70-1.72, 50d 0.94 / 200d 1.15 — so $460M/391.5M = $1.175/sh, and the stated ~$1.18 vs $0.895 gap is arithmetically real. The line's own caveat is the correct one and survives: this is NOT a lockable spread, because the consideration is unregistered-until-S-4 equity in a privately marked $2.5B biotech with no observable price, so the "discount" is just the market haircutting a promotional private mark plus vote/close risk. Residual disqualifiers the line does not flag: sub-$1 tape against Nasdaq's $1.00 minimum bid (LAB has traded below $1 with a 0.70 52wk low — a deficiency notice is live risk before a 2H close), ~$958K daily share volume on a sub-dollar name means the position is size-capped and spread-taxed, and the CVR will be a non-transferable or thinly traded instrument in most such structures. Net: real, dated, forward, company-specific, non-macro, unfired divestiture leg intact — score 6 is fair and I do not raise it, because the payoff is unquantifiable beyond the $50M cap and is denominated in the very equity whose value is unobservable.

catalyst_3.title: Verify
catalyst_3.evidence: Primary source (Clarivate IR/8-K ex-99.1, 2026-07-06) confirms the core: definitive agreement to sell LS&H to Altaris for $600M = $500M cash at close + $25M deferred to TSA completion + $75M seller note, close "by the end of the year," proceeds to "reduce debt," LS&H to discontinued ops from Q3, FY26 outlook reaffirmed ($2.30-2.42B rev, $980M-1.04B adj EBITDA, $365-435M FCF) with a $225-250M non-cash goodwill impairment flagged as outlook-neutral. CORRECTIONS: (a) the "roughly 1.5x net leverage" cut is NOT in the release and is arithmetically implausible - $500M against ~$4.34B debt is ~0.5x gross, and RemainCo simultaneously loses LS&H EBITDA, so net leverage barely improves and could rise; (b) the specific "2028/2029 notes" retirement appears only in secondary coverage, not the primary release, which says only "reduce debt"; (c) the "remaining portfolio rationalization" leg has no named asset, counterparty or date and fails the gates entirely. Tradeability check kills the framing: CLVT traded DOWN ~5.4% on the 2026-07-06 announcement and sits at ~$2.40 vs a $4.77 52-wk high, so this was not a positive re-rate - the remaining forward legs (regulatory close, actual paydown, post-close guidance reset) are real but small, un-dated ("end of the year"), and against a residual A&G/IP business with secular-decline risk.

catalyst_density.rating: H — $500M of cash at close equals roughly a third of the entire $1.53B equity market cap, yet the stock at $2.39 sits below its $2.84 200-day average and near the low end of its $1.66-$4.77 52-week range, so the announcement pop fully round-tripped and the deleveraging is not in the price. This is a leveraged stub where FY26 FCF guidance of $365-435M is itself ~25% of market cap; small changes in net debt swing equity value disproportionately.
catalyst_density.analysis: The signing is fired and re-rated away, but the close, the actual note retirement, and the post-close guidance reset are all still forward and dated within CY2026 — that is the tradeable leg, not the July 6 announcement. Verification confirms every element of the triage claim from the company's own IR release and 8-K: $600M headline, $500M cash, close by year-end, proceeds to debt, FY26 outlook reaffirmed with a $225-250M non-cash goodwill impairment flagged as metric-neutral. The gap I could not close in the lookup budget is the "remaining portfolio rationalization" leg of the triage note — the release only references a generic Value Creation Plan to "rationalize our portfolio" with no second named asset, date, or counterparty, so that piece does not clear the gates on its own and the score rests entirely on the Altaris close. Offsetting the cheapness: the residual Academia & Government and IP businesses carry real secular-decline risk, closing timing is a soft "end of the year" rather than a hard date, and the seller note plus deferred cash mean only $500M of the $600M is certain at close.

candidates.analysis_summary: [SWEEP 8 (FRHC-GTY)] The dated forward event is genuine and specific: an August 2026 rights offering of at least C$575M, fully backstopped by Waterous Energy Fund, whose completion is a closing condition for the C$1.277B Connacher acquisition — so the milestone is structural, not narrative, and has not yet fired. But the trade fails on skew rather than on fact. The raise exceeds Greenfire's entire ~$460M pre-deal equity value, and the backstop hands every unsubscribed share to a holder already at ~72% at a 15% discount, meaning the minority's realistic outcomes are "pay up to stand still" or "be diluted at a controller-set price" — the controller owns the option, and terms that matter most (record date, final price, ratio, any minority protections) are still undetermined. Holding at WATCH/5 rather than promoting: revisit when the offering circular fixes the record date and subscription terms, which is the point at which minority treatment becomes assessable; the gap in this verification is that no circular exists yet, so the actual dilution math cannot be computed.

valuation.valuation_basis: BARBELL on ANKTIVA+BCG sBLA LABEL-EXPANSION to BCG-unresponsive papillary-only NMIBC; FDA-accepted, PDUFA Jan-6-2027 (verified, ImmunityBio PR). NOT a survival binary: ANKTIVA is ALREADY FDA-approved/commercial in CIS NMIBC -> drug, manufacturing & safety established; this is a regulatory extrapolation decision (CIS->papillary, QUILT-3.032 Cohort B + literature bridge). win_prob 0.55 = label-expansion approval rates ~70-80% for already-approved drugs, DISCOUNTED because efficacy rests on single-arm extrapolation not a randomized confirmatory trial (contested), but FDA's acceptance signals the bridge is reviewable. target_on_win $10.00 (papillary ~triples NMIBC TAM vs CIS-only; re-rate toward prior optimism, 52wk-high $12.43; ~1,047M sh). downside_on_loss $5.00 (CRL keeps CIS franchise + $380.9M cash/STI and a confirmatory-trial path; net debt $919M Oberland royalty). EV = .55*10 + .45*5 = $7.75 -> +8% vs ref $7.175 (mkt already prices most of it).
valuation.prob_basis: Label-expansion of an already-approved drug (base rate ~70-80%) discounted to 0.55 for extrapolation-based (non-randomized) efficacy bridge from CIS to papillary; FDA sBLA acceptance is a partial de-risk.

Gap in verification: within the ~6-lookup budget I could not identify a disclosed trigger for the mid-July widening (no announced extension, termination notice, or NYDFS denial surfaced), so the market may be reacting to unreported regulatory signaling — that unresolved "why" is the reason this is a 6 rather than the flagged 8, and it should be re-checked against any 8-K or amended outside-date disclosure before sizing.

catalyst_2.title: Milestone
catalyst_2.description: June 24, 2026 joint update: 51 of 52 US state/territory regulators plus all international jurisdictions cleared, one US state (NYDFS) pending; next hard date = merger-agreement outside date August 10, 2026, extendable to November 10, 2026 if money-transmitter/antitrust clearances remain outstanding.

catalyst_3.title: Verify
catalyst_3.evidence: The line's own admitted gap ("could not identify a disclosed trigger for the mid-July widening") is fillable and it is adverse: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani formally wrote to NYDFS — the single remaining approver — urging it to use its remittance-licensing authority to BLOCK the Western Union/Intermex deal on immigrant-fee/competition grounds (Semafor/American Banker/Finextra/GCR, May 13-14, 2026), after federal antitrust declined a second request. So the last approval is not a procedural rubber-stamp; it is a discretionary state regulator under active, public political pressure to deny, which is exactly what a 19.2% gross spread on an otherwise-cleared all-cash deal prices. Second correction: the merger agreement's outside date is not a hard Aug 10, 2026 terminal — May 11, 2026 auto-extended to Aug 10, 2026 and extends again to Nov 10, 2026 for regulatory/money-transmitter-approval conditions, so the "near-terminal, August-dated" framing is wrong; the true tail is November, with reciprocal break fees ($27.3m WU antitrust / $19.8m IMXI). Everything else checks out against primary sources: $16.00/share all-cash, stockholder-approved, 51 of 52 US money-transmission regulators plus all international jurisdictions cleared per the June 24, 2026 joint WU/Intermex release with only NYDFS outstanding; tape verified at exactly $13.42 (-2.8% on the day, 50d $14.78, 200d $15.24, 52w low $8.58), gross spread 19.2%. Net: catalyst is real, forward and idiosyncratic, but the binary is political-discretionary rather than procedural, the timing anchor is soft (Nov 10 tail = 4 more months of carry), and the sub-$11 break floor is now a live scenario rather than a tail — reward/risk ~1.1x does not compensate for handicapping a mayor-vs-regulator fight. Downgrade 6 to 5; do not size on the "clean near-terminal spread" thesis.

candidates.analysis_summary: [SWEEP 12 (MBVI-NBIX)] The catalyst is genuinely real, dated, forward and unfired: FDA accepted the zilurgisertib NDA in FOP under Priority Review with a September 26, 2026 PDUFA, and it is not a macro bet. But it fails on asymmetry twice over. First, the de-risking event already fired — positive pivotal Phase 2 PROGRESS data (Cohort 1 primary endpoint, new HO lesions at Week 24 by whole-body CT) read out positive and were presented at ENDO 2026 in June; MIRM jumped ~15% on the data and now trades at $118.86 against a 52-week range of $50.25-$130, i.e. near the high after a ~135% re-rate, so approval is broadly consensus and the PDUFA is a low-payoff confirmation rather than a coin-flip. Second, the triage note's own objection is decisive: management guides zilurgisertib to only >$200M global peak sales against a $6.0B market cap and $660-680M of 2026 product-sales guidance (Q1 2026 net product sales $159.9M, LIVMARLI $113.8M, +55% y/y), so even a clean approval moves NAV a few percent while a CRL is the larger tail — negative skew. The bigger value driver by management's and sell-side framing is volixibat in PSC/PBC (~$1.7B unadjusted peak), which is a different, undated lane. Gap: I did not verify the exact NDA-acceptance date or the undisclosed Incyte royalty/milestone economics, which would only further dilute Mirum's share of the FOP payoff, not improve it.

valuation.valuation_basis: Dated forward binary on the Q3-2026 rusfertide PDUFA (Priority Review granted 2026-03-02; NDA filed by partner Takeda). Approval mechanically unlocks Protagonist's already-exercised (Apr-2026) opt-out ladder: +$200M on approval +$75M milestone = +$275M cash (~+$4.28/sh on 64.3M sh), plus worldwide royalties 14-29% on $1-2B peak-sales rusfertide and up to $975M total milestone ladder. WIN ($118): clean approval de-risks the royalty NPV + banks $275M -> re-rates to the sell-side high (avg target $101.92, high $118; 11 Buy/1 Hold). LOSS ($62): a CRL strips rusfertide but PTGX retains ~$2.86/sh net cash (cash+ST inv $547.8M + LT inv $72.8M, net cash ~$184M incl. the $200M opt-out already received) plus the J&J-partnered icotrokinra (Phase 3 psoriasis/IBD) + obesity pipeline, which underpin ~low-$60s ex-rusfertide -> ~analyst low ($65). BARBELL: EV = 0.88x118 + 0.12x62 = $111.28 (~+14.6% vs $97.135). Sources: Takeda/Protagonist NDA-acceptance PR (BusinessWire/Takeda, 2026-03-01); opt-out PR (StockTitan/BioSpace, Apr-2026); VERIFY Ph3 (77% vs 33% response, ASH-2025); Q1-2026 10-Q balance sheet.
valuation.prob_basis: Calibrated ~0.88 for FDA approval at the Q3-2026 PDUFA: Phase 3 VERIFY hit hard (77% vs 33% response, met key secondaries incl. phlebotomy reduction) on top of 4-yr REVIVE/THRIVE safety; carries Breakthrough + Priority Review + Fast Track + Orphan; first-in-class hepcidin mimetic with mechanism de-risked by years of Phase 2; partner Takeda (large-cap) filed and committed. ~90% is the empirical approval rate for BTD assets with a positive pivotal under Priority Review; small haircut for first-in-class novelty/CMC. Sources: VERIFY/ASH-2025 data; FDA Priority-Review grant 2026-03-02.

Barbell. EV = 0.35*60 + 0.65*10 = $27.5 vs ref $33.345 -> NEGATIVE expected value at this price (stock rich into a low-POS coin-flip).

catalyst_3.evidence: Every load-bearing fact checks out against primary/near-primary sources: TI/Silicon Labs press releases and SLAB 8-K confirm a signed all-cash $231.00/share merger (~$7.5B EV, Caldwell Merger Corp.) announced 2026-02-04; the DEFM14A/8-K confirm stockholder approval at the 2026-04-30 special meeting (78.52% quorum); MLex reports the SAMR filing was still NOT formally accepted as of 2026-06-11, and no acceptance has been reported since. (3) Price is stale: SLAB last ~$218.6 (12 Jul), so gross spread is ~5.7% ($12.4), not 6.2% off $217.47 — roughly 5-7% annualized to a 1H27 close, i.e. low-single-digit real edge after the twice-extendable outside date. Tradeable (liquid US large-cap common, cash arb correctly chosen over decaying calls), no hidden disqualifier, but this is a low-return probability trade mispositioned as a score-6 catalyst; scored 5.

CRITICAL re-frame: BBIO is NOT a cash-barbell biotech — net debt ~$2.5B (royalty/term debt funding launch), negative book equity per FMP 3/31/26 BS (totalDebt $3.385B, cash+inv ~$1.00B). The DOWNSIDE FLOOR is therefore the standalone value of the ALREADY-APPROVED, launched acoramidis/Attruby ATTR-CM franchise (FY25 net rev $362.4M, Q1-26 rev $194.5M annualizing ~$700M+, bull peak >$3B) plus infigratinib (achondroplasia NDA Q3-26) — not cash/sh. BBP-418 is incremental optionality on a de-risked commercial core ('convergence': the big asset already cleared). win_prob 0.85 = Priority Review + positive pivotal + first-in-disease unmet need. target_on_win $105 = FMP consensus $105.21 (median $100); downside_on_loss $58 ~ franchise-only value on a BBP-418 CRL (modest pipeline haircut, near pre-catalyst/200d avg $66.6, franchise intact). EV% barbell: 0.85*(105-67.25)+0.15*(58-67.25) = +$30.7/sh (~+46%). reference_rr=(105-67.25)/(67.25-58)=4.08.
valuation.prob_basis: Priority Review granted (FDA acceptance May 27 2026) + positive Ph3 FORTIFY interim (2.6pt NSAD, p<0.05, benefit across all subgroups) + first/only therapy for any LGMD form (high unmet need favors approval). Haircut from ~0.90 reflects single-pivotal + accelerated-pathway label/CMC risk.

valuation.valuation_basis: BARBELL on the MAPLE-HCM sNDA, PDUFA 11/14/2026 (FDA accepted, standard review; CYTK PR/8-K). KEY: aficamten/MYQORZO is ALREADY APPROVED & LAUNCHED (US live ~680 starts Q1'26; EU/Germany 6/1/26), so this is a LABEL-EXPANSION (monotherapy vs metoprolol head-to-head), NOT a cash-vs-approval binary — a miss does NOT zero the drug, it keeps selling. win_prob 0.83 (label expansion on an already-approved molecule with POSITIVE MAPLE-HCM topline; prob_basis below). target_on_win $85: first-line monotherapy label accelerates the launch + ACACIA-HCM nHCM optionality, re-rate toward 52wk high $80.2 and above. downside_on_loss $56: lose the monotherapy label premium but drug still approved/commercial (liquidity ~$1,074M cash+investments offsets ~$1,041M converts, so floor is the base launch trajectory, NOT cash). EV = 0.83x85 + 0.17x56 = $80.07 vs ref $68.96 = +16.1% expected return. Asymmetric to the UPSIDE with capped downside since approval already in hand.
valuation.prob_basis: Label-expansion sNDA on an already-FDA-approved drug; MAPLE-HCM met its endpoints (monotherapy vs metoprolol), standard review with 11/14/26 PDUFA; label-expansions on approved molecules with positive Ph3 historically clear ~80-85%

candidates.analysis_summary: [SWEEP 6 (DAKT-ENOV)] The triage note is factually correct and the catalyst survives the strict gate: it is real, specific, dated to 2026-07-24, forward, and not macro. But it fails the instrument test — DSX is the bidder, and the note itself concedes the asymmetry sits on the target. The structure is unusually adverse for the acquirer: a $253M-cap company bidding for a $1.05bn target on $1.412bn of committed bank debt, with the equity stub of the consideration marked to DSX's own falling shares, so DSX weakness mechanically cheapens its own bid while raising pro-forma leverage risk. With only 29.7% tendered against a unanimous board rejection and a separate non-binding stock-and-cash proposal still under Genco board review, the most likely July 24 outcome is a third extension rather than a clean resolution — meaning the "dated" milestone is soft. Downgrading from the triage score of 6 to 4 and holding WATCH: worth tracking the July 24 print, but the correct expression, if any, is GNK, not DSX.

candidates.analysis_summary: [SWEEP 9 (GVA-IMTX)] Verified: FDA accepted the varegacestat NDA on 08-Jul-2026 with a PDUFA target action date of 28-Apr-2027 (standard review), backed by Ph3 RINGSIDE showing an 84% reduction in progression/death risk (HR ~0.16) and 56% vs 9% ORR in 156 randomized patients; an EMA MAA is committed by end-2026. The catalyst is real, dated and forward, but the asymmetry is muted on three counts: the efficacy uncertainty is already resolved, the date is ~9 months out with no intervening value event, and varegacestat would be the second gamma-secretase inhibitor to market behind SpringWorks' Ogsiveo (approved 2023), so the debate is commercial share rather than approval risk. At a $2.1B cap trading near 52-week highs after a ~2.6x run, approval looks substantially discounted; the residual edge would be a negative surprise (CRL/label restriction) rather than upside, which is the wrong shape for a long catalyst position.

Verification gap: I did not pull the 8-K text or a current price/consensus, so the degree to which the Berry accretion is already in estimates is inferred from the press release rather than measured.

candidates.edge: L — the buyout schedule, 2026 guidance ($1.75-1.95B EBITDA, $600-700M FCFBG) and the 2.1GW-through-2030 repowering plan were all laid out at the Feb 10, 2026 Q4 call and are in consensus; the stock has already re-rated +42%, and management explicitly declined to commit to buybacks or restarting distributions "over the next five years," removing the single event that would force a re-rate.
candidates.instrument: common equity
candidates.analysis_summary: [SWEEP 20 (WF-ZYME)] There is a genuine dated, forward, sized deleveraging step — the first partial CEPF 5 call in H2 2026 at roughly $150M, followed by ~$470M in 2027 and the CEPF 3 call/asset-sale decision in 2027 — so this clears the "real and datable" bar but only barely. The problem is edge: every one of these figures came from the company's own February 2026 guidance, the milestone is a routine self-funded capital-structure step rather than a discrete surprise, and with the units already up 42% the deleveraging narrative is at least partly in the price. Critically, the terminal catalyst (distribution restart) has been explicitly disowned for five years, so the equity has no dated event that converts deleveraging into a payout — it is a slow grind, not a catalyst trade. Gap: I could not confirm from the primary 8-K/10-Q (SEC fetch 403'd) whether a precise calendar date for the CEPF 5 call has been disclosed; the H2-2026 timing is from Q4-call reporting.
